title: Mastering Notification Systems
summary: This lesson teaches how to select the appropriate UI surface for notifications based on message severity. It covers the lifecycle, persistence, and stacking behavior of toasts, banners, modals, and badges.

transcript.text: Notifications are a system. Pick wrong, users tune out.
Toast slides in the corner. Banner takes the full top. Modal blocks everything. Badge just sits there.
Same content. Four different volumes. Pick the volume that matches the message.
A new message? Toast. Server is degraded? Banner. Card declined? Modal. Three unread comments? Badge.
How they live and die. Toast auto-dismiss in four seconds.
Add an undo for destructive actions. Banners stay until users click X.
Modals demand a choice before anything else moves. Badges wait quietly until cleared.
Persistence is part of the contract. Three toasts? They breathe in a stack.
Three modals? Train wreck. Mixed surfaces by severity, never by habit.
Follow for more UI systems. Save this for your next dashboard.

design_principles: Match notification volume to message severity
Use auto-dismiss for low-priority toasts (e.g., 4 seconds)
Include 'Undo' for destructive actions in toasts
Banners should persist until manual dismissal
Modals must block interaction until a choice is made
Stack toasts vertically to maintain readability
before_after: Comparison between a clean stack of three toasts ('Breathe') versus an overlapping, unusable stack of three modals ('Trainwreck').
